**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of about 250-300 words on ONE of the following topics.

**Topic 1.** What are the merits and demerits of tourism in your country?
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
La rédaction anglaise du BAC série A sanctionne à la fois le respect du format imposé (essai d'opinion, discours, lettre) et la qualité du contenu : un texte au contenu riche mais rédigé dans le mauvais format perd des points que ni les idées ni la grammaire ne peuvent compenser. Le sujet proposant un choix, un seul texte doit être rédigé le jour de l'examen ; les modèles ci-dessous illustrent chacun des trois sujets proposés pour couvrir l'ensemble du barème.

## Topic 1 - Opinion essay: Tourism (modèle, environ 270 mots)

Tourism can be defined as the activity of travelling to and visiting places of interest, whether for leisure, culture, or discovery. In Cameroon, often described as "Africa in miniature" because of its varied landscapes, tourism holds considerable promise, but it also comes with certain drawbacks.

Among its merits, tourism is first and foremost a source of income: visitors spend money on accommodation, transport, food and souvenirs, which benefits local businesses and creates employment for guides, hoteliers and craftsmen. Secondly, tourism promotes cultural exchange, allowing visitors to discover local traditions, festivals and cuisine, while giving host communities the opportunity to share and take pride in their heritage. Thirdly, tourism can fund the protection of natural sites: revenue from national parks, for instance, can be reinvested into wildlife conservation.

However, tourism also has its demerits. It can lead to the degradation of natural sites when visitor numbers are not properly managed, as litter, pollution and overuse damage fragile ecosystems. It may also encourage the erosion of local cultures, as communities alter their traditions to fit tourist expectations rather than preserving them authentically. Finally, the benefits of tourism are not always fairly distributed, often enriching foreign tour operators or a small local elite while ordinary residents see little improvement in their living conditions.

In conclusion, tourism represents a genuine opportunity for Cameroon's economic and cultural development, provided that it is carefully regulated to protect both the environment and local communities from its less desirable effects.

**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of about 250-300 words on ONE of the following topics.

**Topic 2.** As the best student of your school, you have been asked to give a speech to your schoolmates on the causes of indiscipline that lead to failure in examinations, and to suggest solutions. Your school is Government Bilingual High School Bamukumbit.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 2 - Speech (modèle, environ 260 mots)

Ladies and gentlemen,

I stand before you today, as a student of this institution, to address a problem that concerns us all: indiscipline, and the failure it so often brings in its wake.

Indiscipline in our school takes many forms: lateness, absenteeism, disrespect towards teachers, and a general lack of seriousness towards our studies. These behaviours are rarely harmless. A student who is repeatedly late misses crucial lessons; one who disrespects teachers loses access to the guidance those teachers are trying to offer; one who neglects assignments falls further behind with every passing week. It is therefore no surprise that indiscipline and academic failure so often go hand in hand.

What can we do about it? First, each of us must take personal responsibility for our own conduct, rather than waiting for punishment to correct our behaviour. Second, I propose that our school reinforce peer mentorship, pairing younger, less disciplined students with older ones who can model good habits. Third, I encourage our teachers and administration to recognise and reward good conduct publicly, not only punish poor conduct, so that discipline is seen as something to aspire to rather than merely to fear.

Ladies and gentlemen, Government Bilingual High School Bamukumbit can only reach its full potential if discipline becomes a shared value rather than an imposed rule. Let us each resolve, starting today, to be part of the solution.

Thank you.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of about 250-300 words on ONE of the following topics.

**Topic 3.** What are the causes, forms and consequences of violence in the world today?
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 3 - Opinion essay: Violence (modèle, environ 280 mots)

Violence, understood as the deliberate use of physical or psychological force to harm, coerce or intimidate others, remains one of the most troubling features of the contemporary world.

Its causes are numerous. Poverty and unemployment breed frustration, which can erupt into violent behaviour, particularly among idle youths with few prospects. Political instability and the struggle for power fuel armed conflicts and civil unrest in many regions. Cultural and religious intolerance, when exploited by extremist groups, transforms ordinary disagreements into violent confrontations. Finally, the normalisation of violence in media and entertainment can desensitise young people to its consequences.

Violence today takes many forms: armed conflict and terrorism, domestic and gender-based violence within homes, bullying and cyberbullying among young people, and structural violence embedded in unjust social and economic systems.

The consequences of this violence are severe and far-reaching. On the human level, it causes death, injury and lasting psychological trauma to victims and witnesses alike. On the social level, it destroys trust within communities and can tear apart the social fabric for generations. On the economic level, violence disrupts education, destroys infrastructure and diverts resources away from development towards security and reconstruction.

In conclusion, violence in today's world stems from a complex mix of economic, political and social factors, and its consequences extend well beyond its immediate victims. Addressing it requires not only security measures, but also long-term investment in education, economic opportunity and social justice.

### Piège à éviter
L'erreur la plus fréquente est de traiter un sujet de discours (Topic 2) comme un essai impersonnel, en oubliant l'apostrophe à l'auditoire ("Ladies and gentlemen") et la formule de clôture ("Thank you") : le format du discours exige une adresse directe et un ton persuasif du début à la fin.

### Conseil
Avant de rédiger, note au brouillon un plan en trois parties (introduction/thèse, développement en 2-3 arguments illustrés, conclusion) : ce plan minimal, quel que soit le sujet choisi, structure la copie et évite le hors-sujet ou la répétition d'idées.
